rules: Rule 1 (bar marks): two distinct marks. TILDE = short stroke starting with a small down-hook at the left, then a wave or a nearly flat/arched rise, usually with an up-tick at the right; its shape varies continuously from clear ~ to flat arc and is one mark. MACRON = crisp straight horizontal bar, no hook, set higher: only 81 (R3) and 8 (R16). All other bars, including A's 'macron'/'macron?' and B's 'macron?' (47, 66, 67, 75, 77, 30, 20; B's 64|macron? shows no bar at all), are tilde. Rule 2 (dots): the plain 1 of this hand is an undotted short stroke (16, 18, 21, 31, 51, 19 without marks everywhere), so a dot over a 1 is a cipher mark, not the letterform. No clean single-dot mark exists anywhere: every 'dot' checked at 4x on other digits (30, 96, 67, 69, 87) shows two dots, often very faint. So single 'dot' = diaeresis with one dot faint or merged; all 'dot' tokens become diaeresis, with '?' when only one dot is seen. Rule 3 (symbols, one name per distinct sign): pi = short form, wide bar on two short splayed legs, sitting low (L5, L16, L18 '83 pi', R1, R3, insertion); Pi = tall 'TT' form with long parallel legs (L10, L18 '21 Pi', L20, L21, R22). Shapes are consistent, so kept apart (they may still be one cipher sign). w = two minims + tail (L5, L15 '78 w 48', R1); m = three minims + tail (L14 '78 m 65', L17, L18, R5, R7). sigma = closed loop with a long stroke leaving the top rightwards and curling up and back (L11, R3); mars = closed loop with a straight diagonal up-right stroke ending in an arrowhead/tick (L20, R7 as mars?). No '6' sign token remains: both former single '6' tokens are sigma. Rule 4: line-end dash and hook fillers (after 'par' R2, after 'vn' R14) are not transcribed; the low '2' at the end of left L16 ('x psi 2') is kept as a cipher 2 with '?' (2-shaped, preceded by the token dot, but lower and with no trailing dot). The '+' signe de renvoi is not a cipher sign. Rule 5: '?' is cleared where the other independent pass read the same mark firmly, or where the only doubt was tilde vs macron (now settled by Rule 1).
